description: Use case: the Swiss popular vote of 29 November 2026 on the federal decree on the additional financing of the AHV by an increase of the value added tax, the partial financing of the 13th AHV pension, as shown by the system view 'Calculator' for the phrase 'AHV financing vote'. The 13th AHV pension is paid in December 2026 whatever the outcome; the decree raises the normal VAT rate by 0.4 percentage points from 8.1 to 8.5 percent from 2028 and brings the AHV about 1.4 billion CHF a year. The page compares, for a household the reader describes by its spending at the normal rate and its wage income, the annual cost of the yes path (the extra VAT plus an optional indirect economic cost) with the cost of a no path the reader shapes: the share of the same revenue replaced by payroll contributions, the share replaced by savings in the federal budget and the rest left unfunded and taken from the AHV fund, weighted as the reader says. The verdict is yes if the VAT is cheaper for the household by more than a threshold, no if dearer, undecided in between. Side results are the coverage of the 13th pension, the pay-as-you-go deficit of 2030, the AHV fund of 2035 and the share of the new revenue paid by pensioner households. The worked example is the ESTV average household with 4'050 CHF a month of normal-rate spending and 8'000 CHF of wage income, a no path of 50 percent payroll contributions, 25 percent federal savings and 25 percent unfunded. The arguments of both sides, the presets, the labels, the hints, the tags, the verdict texts, the sensitivity grid and the sources of the page are the calculator triples and values of 'AHV financing vote'. The page caps the two replacement shares at 100 percent and switches the replacement revenue off in 2030 if it starts later; the cap is not needed with the example inputs and the switch is stored as a modelled flag; all other results are formulas of the file and reproduced by the calc-validation. The inputs that are not measured carry the word assumed and a confidence. State of the data: BSV vote page of 5 October 2026, financial perspectives of 2 July 2026, polls of October 2026.

triples.name: AHV financing vote hint
triples.description: The Swiss electorate decides on the federal decree on the additional financing of the AHV by an increase of the value added tax. The 13th AHV pension, accepted by 58 % of the voters in March 2024, is paid for the first time in December 2026 to 2.6 million pensioners whatever the outcome; it costs 4.2 billion CHF in 2026 and more than 5 billion CHF a year from 2035. Parliament decided in June 2026 to cover part of it by raising the normal VAT rate by 0.4 percentage points from 8.1 to 8.5 %, the hotel rate from 3.8 to 4.0 % and leaving the reduced rate of 2.6 % on food, medicines, books and newspapers unchanged; the Federal Council had asked for 0.7 points and the Council of States for 0.4 points plus 0.2 points of payroll contributions, a cut of the federal contribution was rejected by both chambers [1][4]. A VAT change amends the constitution, so the people and the cantons vote. The increase would apply from 2028 at the earliest and bring the AHV about 1.4 billion CHF a year from 2029, with the federal contribution roughly half of the cost of the 13th pension [1][2]. The Federal Council, the National Council (108 to 85) and the Council of States (28 to 13), the SP, the Greens, the Centre, the GLP, the EVP and the unions' federation SGB say yes; the FDP, the SVP, the employers, the trades and the public service union VPOD say no; the first polls put the opponents slightly ahead [6][8][9][10]. Below are the arguments of both sides with their numbers, then a calculator: say what you spend and earn, say how a no would be paid for instead, and see whether the VAT or the alternative costs your household more - and what that suggests for your vote.

triples.name: AHV financing vote model limits
triples.description: one year of operation around 2030 in prices of 2025, no growth of spending or wages, no hotel rate, no VAT paid indirectly through businesses that cannot deduct it (banks, insurers, hospitals, the public sector), no investment return of the fund, no behavioural change of consumers, no structural reform as a way of a no (a higher retirement age is a cost in years of work, not in francs); the BSV financial perspectives and the ESTV estimate are the places to look for these effects

formulas.description: the part of the extra VAT revenue that nothing replaces on the no path and the fund carries

formulas.name: payroll points formula
formulas.description: the contribution rate needed for the payroll share: the replaced amount divided by the revenue per point of contributions

formulas.name: extra VAT formula
formulas.description: what the household pays: the monthly spending at the normal rate times twelve, times the increase in points divided by 100 and by one plus the normal rate (the increase is applied to the net price, the spending includes today's 8.1 %), times the pass-through to prices

formulas.name: payroll cost formula
formulas.description: the wage income times twelve, times the payroll points divided by 100, times the share of the contribution that falls on the employee's pocket

formulas.name: federal cost formula
formulas.description: the amount replaced from the federal budget in billion CHF times the household's share of a billion of federal savings

formulas.name: deferred cost formula
formulas.description: the unfunded amount divided by the number of households, times the weight the reader gives to a franc missing in the fund; billion CHF divided by million households gives thousand CHF, so the factor 1000

formulas.name: yes cost formula
formulas.description: the annual cost of the yes path for the household: the extra VAT plus the indirect cost

formulas.name: no cost formula
formulas.description: the annual cost of the no path for the household: the payroll cost plus the federal cost plus the deferred cost

formulas.name: household cost difference formula
formulas.description: the annual cost of the yes path minus the annual cost of the no path; a negative difference means the VAT is the cheaper way for the household

formulas.name: bottom line yes formula
formulas.description: the 13th pension the household receives minus its cost on the yes path
formulas.expression: "bottom line yes" = "13th AHV pension received" - "yes cost"

formulas.name: bottom line no formula
formulas.description: the 13th pension the household receives minus its cost on the no path
formulas.expression: "bottom line no" = "13th AHV pension received" - "no cost"

formulas.name: federal contribution to the 13th pension formula
formulas.description: the federal share of the AHV expenditure times the cost of the 13th pension
formulas.expression: "federal contribution to the 13th pension" = "13th AHV pension","cost" * "federal contribution"

formulas.name: coverage yes formula
formulas.description: the share of the 13th pension that is paid for on the yes path: the federal contribution plus the extra VAT revenue, divided by the cost of the 13th pension
formulas.expression: "pension coverage","yes scenario" = ( "federal contribution to the 13th pension" + "extra VAT revenue" ) / "13th AHV pension","cost"

formulas.name: coverage no formula
formulas.description: the share of the 13th pension that is paid for on the no path: the federal contribution plus the replacement revenue, divided by the cost of the 13th pension
formulas.expression: "pension coverage","no scenario" = ( "federal contribution to the 13th pension" + "payroll revenue" + "federal savings" ) / "13th AHV pension","cost"

formulas.name: deficit yes formula
formulas.description: the pay-as-you-go deficit of 2030 without extra financing minus the extra VAT revenue

formulas.name: deficit no formula
formulas.description: the pay-as-you-go deficit of 2030 without extra financing minus the replacement revenue if it has started by 2030; the replacement starts 2028 plus the years of delay, the flag replacement active is 1 if that is 2030 or earlier and 0 otherwise
formulas.expression: "pay-as-you-go deficit","no scenario" = "pay-as-you-go deficit","2030" - ( "payroll revenue" + "federal savings" ) * "replacement active"

formulas.name: replacement years formula
formulas.description: the years the replacement revenue flows until the end of 2035: 2036 minus the start year, which is 2028 plus the delay; the page takes zero if the delay is longer than eight years

formulas.name: fund no formula
formulas.description: the fund of 2035 with the VAT is the BSV figure; without it the BSV figure without extra financing plus the replacement revenue times the years it has flowed until 2035, divided by the expenditure of 2035
formulas.expression: "AHV fund","no scenario","2035" = "AHV fund","no scenario","2035","BSV" + ( "payroll revenue" + "federal savings" ) * "replacement years" / "expenditure","2035"

formulas.name: generation share formula
formulas.description: the share of the new revenue paid by pensioner households on the no path: their share of normal-rate consumption for the federal budget, zero for payroll contributions; the unfunded part is left out because nobody has paid it yet; on the yes path the share is their consumption share
formulas.expression: "generation share","no scenario" = "federal share" * "consumption share" / ( "payroll share" + "federal share" )

formulas.name: break-even spending formula
formulas.description: the normal-rate spending at which the cost difference is zero: the cost of the no path minus the indirect cost, divided by twelve times the increase over one plus the normal rate times the pass-through

formulas.name: payroll yield formula
formulas.description: the revenue of one percentage point of payroll contributions: the AHV income of 2025 times the share of the contributions in it, divided by the contribution rate in percentage points

sources.name: BSV vote page 13th AHV pension
sources.description: Bundesamt für Sozialversicherungen BSV: 13. AHV-Rente: Volksabstimmung über die AHV-Zusatzfinanzierung durch eine Erhöhung der Mehrwertsteuer, 5 October 2026. 2.6 million pensioners, up to 2'520 CHF more a year for singles and 3'780 CHF for couples; cost over 4 billion CHF in 2026, over 5 billion from 2035; AHV income 2025 about 55 billion CHF, contributions about 70 %, Confederation over 20 %, VAT and casino levy about 9 %; the Confederation pays over 800 million and later over 1 billion of the 13th pension; deficit over 1 billion in 2026 and almost 5 billion in 2035 without extra revenue; normal rate 8.1 to 8.5 %, hotel rate 3.8 to 4 %, reduced rate 2.6 % unchanged; about 1.4 billion CHF a year from 2029; deficit 2035 about 3 instead of 5 billion; fund 2035 just under 70 % instead of about 50 % of a year's expenditure; in force at the earliest 2028, no extra financing for 2026 and 2027; reform AHV2030 to Parliament in spring 2027.

sources.name: BSV financial perspectives July 2026
sources.description: BSV: Neue Finanzperspektiven der Sozialwerke: weitere Verschlechterung bei der IV, press release, Bern, 2 July 2026. AHV reference scenario: pay-as-you-go deficit 1.3 billion CHF in 2026 rising to 4.9 billion in 2035 at prices of 2025, cost of the 13th pension about 4 billion; with 0.4 points of VAT from 2028 the deficit of 2030 halves from about 2.7 to about 1.2 billion CHF; the VAT and the federal contribution cover the 13th pension about half.

sources.name: Federal Council recommendation 5 October 2026
sources.description: Der Bundesrat: Bundesrat empfiehlt Ja zur Erhöhung der Mehrwertsteuer für die 13. AHV-Rente, press release, 5 October 2026. Additional cost of the 13th pension at first over 4 billion and from 2035 over 5 billion CHF a year; VAT increase could enter into force at the beginning of 2028.

sources.name: Parliament Q&A financing 13th AHV pension June 2026
sources.description: Parlamentsdienste / sda: Fragen und Antworten zur Finanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente, 19 June 2026. Cost 4.2 billion CHF in 2026, about 4.5 billion in 2030, about 5.4 billion in 2040; VAT brings about 1 billion in 2028 and about 1.4 billion from 2030; the Federal Council had asked for 0.7 points, the Council of States for 0.4 points plus 0.2 points of payroll contributions; both chambers rejected a cut of the federal contribution, which pays over 900 million CHF of the 13th pension in 2030; the GLP decided the VAT increase; the AHV 2030 consultation contains scenarios with more VAT and higher payroll contributions.

sources.name: blue News ESTV household burden
sources.description: blue News (Petar Marjanović): Rechne nach: So viel zahlst du bei einem Ja zur Mehrwertsteuer für die AHV, 19 October 2026. Estimate of the Federal Tax Administration ESTV: an average household with about 9'900 CHF of income pays about 15 CHF a month more, households up to 4'600 CHF about 7 CHF, the middle class (6'700 to 9'400 CHF) about 13 CHF, households above 13'400 CHF about 28 CHF; singles 6 to 18 CHF, pensioner households 7 to 25 CHF; the ESTV uses the spending and prices of 2018/19 and assumes full pass-through; the VAT brings the AHV 1.5 billion CHF a year, about a third of the 4.5 billion the 13th pension costs; examples: coffee 5 CHF +2 Rp, hairdresser 60 CHF +22 Rp, dinner for two 120 CHF +44 Rp, hotel night 180 CHF +35 Rp, smartphone 900 CHF +3.35 CHF; the FDP cites a BAK Economics study with output 3.6 billion CHF lower after ten years and says the Confederation's 90 billion CHF must suffice; farms that do not settle VAT bear the cost themselves.

sources.name: SRF overview financing 13th AHV pension
sources.description: SRF: Auf einen Blick - Finanzierung der 13. AHV-Rente in Kürze, October 2026. The vote of 29 November 2026 on the federal decree; the National Council said yes with 108 to 85 votes and 6 abstentions, the Council of States with 28 to 13 and 3 abstentions; three arguments for: all generations pay including pensioners, socially balanced because food and medicines are exempt, the popular decision must be implemented; three arguments against: structural reform instead of taxes, regressive for low incomes, higher prices weaken demand and burden SMEs.

sources.name: cash FDP campaign launch
sources.description: cash / AWP: FDP startet ihre Kampagne gegen die Erhöhung der Mehrwertsteuer, September 2026. The FDP calls the decree a 'VAT swindle' that takes 1.5 billion CHF from the citizens and finances less than half of the 13th pension; a BAK Economics study commissioned by the FDP puts the growth loss over ten years at almost 3.6 billion CHF and the cost at 545 CHF per household and year; SMEs, retail and restaurants hit hardest; the FDP speaks of salami tactics.

sources.name: Blick yes alliance presentation
sources.description: Blick: Mehrwertsteuer-Erhöhung für 13. AHV: Parteien kämpfen für ein Ja, 13 October 2026. The alliance of SP, Greens, Centre, GLP and EVP; Samira Marti: nine of ten people get more out of the AHV than they pay in, food and medicines are exempt; Pierre-Yves Maillard (SGB): SVP and FDP want to drive the AHV into the red and push a higher retirement age for all, the 4 to 5 billion CHF of extra cost remain; FDP co-president Susanne Vincenz-Stauffacher: the VAT covers the cost only partly.

sources.name: 20 Minuten VPOD says no
sources.description: 20 Minuten: 13. AHV-Rente: VPOD sagt Nein zur Finanzierung und spaltet die Gewerkschaften, 27 October 2026. The VPOD base decided the no with 22 to 6 votes: the AHV is doing well with a record fortune of 60 billion CHF; the union wants payroll contributions instead and argues like the bourgeois opponents with rising rents and premiums; the SGB says the unions stand behind the financing with an overwhelming majority.

sources.name: watson YouGov poll October 2026
sources.description: watson: 13. AHV-Rente: Darum steht die Erhöhung der Mehrwertsteuer auf der Kippe, 23 October 2026. First YouGov poll: 49 % against, 46 % for, 5 % undecided; the opponents slightly ahead with a closed argumentation; the most convincing argument is that the gaps should be closed by structural reform, not by taxes; 54 % find the VAT fair because all generations contribute; older voters support, younger voters reject the increase.

sources.name: compenswiss result 2025
sources.description: compenswiss / BSV: Robuste Performance 2025 von compenswiss bei finanziellen Herausforderungen für AHV und IV, 17 February 2026. Net return 6.34 % in 2025 (2024: 7.33 %), assets under management 50'550 million CHF at the end of 2025 (46'102 million a year earlier), of which 44.8 billion for the AHV including the 10.3 billion debt of the IV; AHV operating result 4.4 billion and pay-as-you-go result 1.8 billion CHF in 2025; liquidity reserves of 2 billion CHF formed for the 13th pension.

sources.name: Parliament National Council debate September 2025
sources.description: Parlamentsdienste / sda: Nationalrat will für 13. AHV-Rente befristet mehr Mehrwertsteuer, 10 September 2025. The National Council decided a temporary VAT increase of 0.7 points against SVP and FDP; the Council of States wanted VAT and payroll contributions; the SP would have preferred payroll contributions, the Greens call them more social; Andri Silberschmidt (FDP): if the fund falls below 90 %, the VAT rises by 0.5 points and the reference age gradually by six months.

sources.name: 20 Minuten Federal Council arguments
sources.description: 20 Minuten: 13. AHV-Rente: Bundesrat will Mehrwertsteuer ab 2028 auf 8,5 % erhöhen, 5 October 2026. Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider presents the arguments: the VAT includes consumption in the financing and does not burden wage income alone, tourists pay too; the Federal Council originally wanted 0.7 points; the FDP fights the decree because households are already burdened by premiums, rents and fuel prices.

sources.name: BFS household scenarios 2025-2055
sources.description: Bundesamt für Statistik BFS: Szenarien zur Entwicklung der Privathaushalte in der Schweiz und in den Kantonen 2025-2055, Statistik aktuell. About 4.0 million private households in 2025, knapp 4.5 million in ten years, 4.7 million in twenty years, between 4.3 and 5.4 million in 2055.

sources.name: swissinfo final vote and social partners
sources.description: swissinfo / Keystone-SDA: Für die 13. AHV-Rente wird die Mehrwertsteuer erhöht, June 2026. Parliament raises the VAT by 0.4 points and renounces payroll contributions; cost 4.2 billion CHF in 2026, 4.5 in 2030, 5.4 in 2040; the employers' association warns of the undesired macroeconomic effects of a permanent VAT increase; the AHV 2030 reform has a scenario with a combined increase of VAT and payroll contributions.

sources.name: Blick shopping tourism
sources.description: Blick (Daniel Ballmer): Tiefere Wertfreigrenze nützt nichts - Schweizer Einkaufstourismus lässt sich nicht bremsen, 2026. Shopping tourism of more than 10 billion CHF a year despite the duty-free limit cut from 300 to 150 CHF in 2025; the euro at a record low of 92 Rappen; Swiss Retail Federation and BAK Economics.
